issues.problem: 'होकर' (becoming) is not in the Sanskrit; prathamo manasvān devo are three nominatives in apposition, as the English has them.
The word is √vyath + -māna; there is no vi- preverb to count separately, and 'vi-√vyath' mislabels the root.
issues.fix: f. acc. sg. pres. part. mid. √vyath

issues.problem: varīyaḥ is a comparative (English 'wider'); 'अत्यन्त' (very) is a different degree and disagrees with the English and the gloss.
Gloss 'him' contradicts its own gram '(part.)' and the note ('īm taken as an emphatic particle'); gloss should say what the note says.
The English and gloss have 'pressing stones yoked' (grāvan); the Hindi drops 'pressing'.

issues.problem: 'than whom' is a comparative sense; the ablative here depends on ṛte ('without whom'), as the note says. Gloss should be the plain ablative.
'भी' (even) is not in acyuta-cyut and not in the English.

patch.old: अचल को भी हिला देता है

issues.problem: 'जैसे' (like) turns the apposition vṛṣabhaḥ 'bull' into a simile; the English has 'a bull'.
śuṣma is 'vigour' in unit 1 (and Hindi बल here); 'fury' is inconsistent and unsupported.
brahma (n.) is 'prayer', Hindi ब्रह्म per the fixed renderings; स्तुति is stoma/praise. vardhana is neuter, so 'बढ़ाने वाला'.
viśvahā is 'every day' (the gloss and the Hindi 'प्रतिदिन' say so); 'always dear' attaches it to priyāsaḥ and changes the sense. Align English with Hindi and gloss.

summary: Reviewed 15 units. 0 errors, 12 minor (all with machine patches). Draft is careful: tokens, splits and case labels are sound; uncertain words (abhyasetām, apadhā, radhra, vija, krandasī) are flagged in notes with medium confidence. Fixes: Hindi additions (होकर, भी, जैसे, अत्यन्त), Hindi omission (pressing stones), Hindi brahma as स्तुति, śuṣma 'fury' vs 'vigour', viśvahā attachment, gloss 'than whom' for yasmāt with ṛte, root label vi-√vyath, īm gloss. No regrouping suggested. Proposal: śuṣma = vigour (बल); viśvahā = every day (प्रतिदिन); krandasī = the two armies (sense uncertain, note).
